questions.q: Why does app-nsg's Allow-From-Web rule use 10.20.1.0/24 (the web subnet) as its source-address-prefixes instead of Internet?
options: So the app subnet only accepts traffic that is already inside the web subnet, enforcing the tier boundary at the network layer
Because NSG rules cannot reference the value Internet under any circumstances
Because 10.20.1.0/24 is required syntax for any rule with priority 100
It has no real effect — NSGs only filter traffic between virtual networks, never within one
questions.explain: Scoping the source to the web subnet's own range means the app tier only trusts traffic that already passed through the web tier, which is the whole point of the multi-tier design.

questions.q: What does scoping the Virtual Machine Contributor role assignment to /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/briarcliff-rg accomplish, versus assigning it at the subscription level?
options: It limits the ops team's VM-management rights to just this resource group instead of every resource group in the subscription
It has no effect on scope — RBAC roles always apply subscription-wide once assigned
It automatically grants the same role to every other resource group with a similar name
Resource-group scope only works for built-in roles, never for custom roles
questions.explain: RBAC scope determines where a role applies; scoping to the resource group keeps the ops team's access limited to Briarcliff's environment rather than the whole subscription.

questions.q: In the az monitor metrics alert create command, what does --window-size 5m combined with the condition avg Percentage CPU > 80 actually trigger on?
options: The alert fires when average CPU stays above 80% across a continuous 5-minute window, not on a single brief spike
The alert fires immediately the first instant CPU crosses 80%, regardless of how long it stays there
The alert checks CPU usage once every 5 months
The window-size parameter only affects how the alert is displayed, not when it fires
questions.explain: The window size defines the time period the average is evaluated over, so a short spike under 5 minutes won't trigger it — sustained high CPU will.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the action group (ops-email-ag) in this lab's alert setup?
options: It defines the actual notification target — who gets emailed — which both the CPU alert and other alerts can reuse
It is the Azure resource that measures CPU usage on the VM
It replaces the need for an NSG on the subnet
It only works with budget alerts, never with metric alerts
questions.explain: An action group is a reusable notification target; the metric alert and the budget alert can both point to the same action group to notify the same people.

questions.q: The budget's notification is set to Actual_GreaterThan_80_Percent on a $150 monthly amount. At roughly what spend does that notification fire?
options: Around $120, which is 80% of the $150 monthly budget
Exactly $150, only once the full budget is spent
At $80, treating the percent value as a dollar amount
It fires once per day regardless of actual spend
questions.explain: 80% of a $150 monthly budget is $120 — crossing that amount triggers the notification before the full budget is exhausted.
